author: NorthEast News Desk
body: North Korea has built a new uranium-enrichment facility at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex, the International Atomic Energy Agency said in a report disclosed Wednesday.

The agency assessed that the two-story building could hold as many as 28 centrifuge cascades. It also reported expanded operations at an annex of the Kangson enrichment site near Pyongyang, pointing to growth in nuclear infrastructure at more than one location.

IAEA inspectors have not had access to North Korea since 2009. The agency said its assessment relies on satellite imagery and other open-source material, including photographs released by North Korean state media after a June visit by leader Kim Jong Un.

The findings do not provide a public measurement of current enriched-uranium output. They document new capacity and operating indicators that the agency considers serious. North Korea says its nuclear status is irreversible and disputes the IAEA’s authority over its program. Additional imagery or official disclosures may refine the assessment, making the development subject to continued monitoring.
dek: The nuclear watchdog says a two-story building at Yongbyon could hold up to 28 centrifuge cascades as infrastructure expands at multiple sites.
headline: IAEA reports new North Korea uranium-enrichment facility
